answers.answer: Build the deck top to bottom as 1 Conflict I, 5 Conflict II, and 4 Conflict III cards. Return all unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Top to bottom: 1x Conflict I, 5x Conflict II, 4x Conflict III.” Return the unused Conflict cards to the box without looking at them.

answers.answer: Each human starts with 2 Agents on their Leader and a third (Swordmaster) beside the board, so 2 are initially available. Each starts with 3 troops in their garrison and 9 in supply, 1 water, and one Influence cube at the bottom of each of the four tracks. Starting VP is 0 in a three-player game and 1 in a four-player game.
answers.evidence: Setup: “Each player places 2 Agents on their Leader” and sets their third Agent next to the board; 3 troops go in the garrison and the rest in supply; each takes 1 water; cubes go on the bottom spaces of the four Influence tracks; Score track is 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0.

answers.answer: Yes. Agent turns are optional, so you may take your Reveal turn while Agents remain. After you Reveal, your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase, so you cannot take another Agent turn. Plot Intrigue can be played only during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns; there is no later own turn in that phase after Revealing.
answers.evidence: Player Turns: “you may take your Reveal turn while you still have Agents left”; after a Reveal turn, “your turns are skipped for the rest of the phase.” Plot Intrigue is playable during one of your own Agent or Reveal turns.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up and use one matching Agent icon to send exactly one Agent to a board space that is unoccupied. A card without an Agent icon cannot be used for an Agent turn, and one card cannot send multiple Agents. Meet the space requirements and pay its costs immediately, before resolving space or card effects; if you cannot pay, you cannot send the Agent there.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: “play one card from your hand face up”; choose only one matching Agent icon and “one card can't send multiple Agents”; the space must be unoccupied; costs are paid “immediately, before resolving any effects.”

answers.answer: No. Conspire's 4-spice entry cost must be paid before the card's Agent box or space effects resolve, so an Agent card's spice gain cannot cover the missing spice when you have only 3. After paying entry costs, you may resolve the board-space effect, card's Agent box, and Faction Influence advancement in any order.
answers.evidence: Agent turn: costs are paid before effects; then gain the board-space effect, card Agent box, and one-space Influence advancement “in any order.” Board-space table: Conspire costs 4 spice.

answers.answer: You can deploy at most 5 troops: all 3 recruited this turn (2 from the space and 1 from the card), plus up to 2 already in your garrison. Any recruited troops not deployed remain in your garrison. Rally Troops is not a Combat space, so its recruits normally go to your garrison and cannot be deployed there.
answers.evidence: Deploying: at a Combat space, deploy “any or all troops you recruited this turn ... plus up to two more troops from your garrison”; recruits not deployed go to the garrison. Rally Troops recruits four and is “not a Combat space.”

answers.answer: The steps are: (1) reveal all cards remaining in your hand, separate from cards played on Agent turns; (2) resolve the Reveal boxes of those revealed cards, in any order; (3) set Combat strength; (4) clean up by putting all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns into your discard pile. Reveal boxes on cards played during Agent turns earlier that round are not used.
answers.evidence: Reveal turn lists four steps; Resolve Reveal Effects specifies boxes “of the cards you just revealed (not of cards played during Agent turns earlier this round)”; Clean Up puts all cards from Agent and Reveal turns into the discard pile.

answers.answer: Yes, you may acquire the replacement card after the Imperium Row is immediately refilled, if you can afford it. Persuasion can be pooled across sources for one card or split across different cards. Unspent Persuasion is lost at the end of the Reveal turn. An acquired card goes to your discard pile and is not used immediately. Its Acquire effect happens once at the moment of acquisition.
answers.evidence: Acquiring cards: the Imperium Row refills immediately, so you may acquire its replacement; Persuasion may be pooled or split and cannot be saved; acquired cards go to discard and “you don't use them right away”; Acquire box effect occurs “at the moment you acquire the card.”

answers.answer: Strength is 10 (3 troops x 2, plus 4 swords). If your last troop in the Conflict is removed, strength becomes 0 and cannot be increased by any means, including swords. For strength over 20, flip the Combat marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Each Conflict troop is worth 2 and each revealed sword 1; with no troops, strength is 0 and cannot be increased by any means, including swords. If over 20, flip to +20 and start again from the beginning.

answers.answer: During Combat, each player with at least one troop in the Conflict may play any number of Combat Intrigue cards or pass. Play proceeds from the First Player clockwise. A pass does not bind later turns: players need to pass consecutively for Combat to resolve. Resolve after all involved players pass consecutively. Play “when you win a Conflict” Intrigue cards only after winning, before the next phase; if one is drawn as a victory reward, it may be played immediately.
answers.evidence: Combat Intrigue: players with a troop may play any number or pass in First Player clockwise order; “not required to pass just because you passed earlier”; resolve after consecutive passes. Win-trigger cards are played after winning, before next phase; a reward-drawn win-trigger may be played immediately.

answers.answer: A and B do not win: each gets the second reward. C and D still compete for the third reward, so C gets it if C has greater strength than D; D gets no reward as the ordinary fourth-place finisher. A tie for second gives the third reward to each tied player, even in two- or three-player games; a tie for third yields nothing. A player with 0 strength gets nothing. After rewards, troops go to each player's supply, not garrison.
answers.evidence: Tied first: nobody wins and each tied player gets the second reward; in a four-player game the other two still compete for third. Tied second gets third reward each; tied third gets nothing; 0 strength gets none; troops return to supply.

answers.answer: Normal spice harvesting happens when an Agent is sent to a Maker space, through that space's effect (base spice plus any accumulated bonus). In Phase 4: Makers, put 1 bonus spice on each of The Great Flat, Hagga Basin, and Imperial Basin that has no Agent. If an Agent moved away before Phase 4 and the space is empty then, bonus spice accumulates there.
answers.evidence: Board-space table gives spice effects for Imperial Basin, Hagga Basin, and The Great Flat; Phase 4 adds 1 spice to each of those three spaces if it has no Agent. Maker-space ruling: if an Agent moves away and it is still empty in Phase 4, bonus spice accumulates.

answers.answer: Reaching 10 VP mid-round does not end the game immediately; the endgame trigger is checked at the end of the round during Recall. The game ends then if any player has 10+ VP or the Conflict Deck is empty. Endgame Intrigue cards resolve before the winner is determined. Tiebreaks, in order, are spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, then the player who most recently took a Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Scoring: game-end trigger is “at the end of a round (Phase 5: Recall)”; first resolve Endgame Intrigue cards, then most VP wins. Tiebreaker list: spice, Solari, water, garrisoned troops, most recent Reveal turn.

answers.answer: The VP for reaching 2 Influence is lost if you drop below 2 and regained if you reach 2 again. The bonus for reaching 4 is kept after dropping below 4 and can be earned again by dropping back and re-advancing. The first player to reach 4 takes the Alliance and its VP; merely tying the holder does not take it. Another player takes it by advancing to a higher space.
answers.evidence: Faction Influence: 2 Influence VP is lost below 2 and regained upon reaching 2 again; the 4 Influence bonus is not returned if you drop below and may be earned again. Alliances: first to 4 takes the token; merely tying does not take it; passing the holder to a higher space transfers it.

answers.answer: If the holder loses 1 Influence while tied at 5 with two opponents, one of the previously tied opponents takes the Alliance; with several tied, the holder chooses which one. If instead the sole player at 4 falls to 3, the holder loses the Alliance; because no other player is at 4 or higher to take it, return it to the board. In either case, losing the Alliance loses its VP.
answers.evidence: If a holder loses Influence while previously tied, the previously tied player takes the token; if several were tied, holder chooses one. Falling to 3 or less loses it; if no player has 4 or more, return it to the board. Losing it loses its VP.

answers.answer: Discarding normally means a card from your hand and sends it to your discard pile. Trashing permanently removes a card from hand, discard pile, or in play to the box; a Reserve card returns to its Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless it is paying a cost or a card instructs you to trash itself. You cannot reshuffle an empty deck early just to inspect its top card; reshuffling is allowed when unable to draw, and the Refocus ruling allows reshuffling if the discard pile is empty.
answers.evidence: Trashing cards: discard means hand card to discard pile; trash removes cards from hand/discard/in play, with Reserve cards returned to Reserve; trashing is optional except as a cost or self-trash instruction. Deck exhaustion says reshuffle when unable to draw and “You can't reshuffle early” to look at an empty deck's top card; FAQ says Refocus reshuffles if discard is empty.

answers.answer: Control is gained by winning a Conflict that rewards control of Arrakeen, Carthag, or Imperial Basin; place your Control marker on that space's flag, replacing any opponent's marker. While you control a space, you receive its bonus whenever any player visits: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Carthag, or 1 spice at Imperial Basin. When a Conflict for a space you already control is revealed, you may deploy one troop from your supply to the Conflict.
answers.evidence: Control: winning the matching Conflict places a marker and replaces any opponent's; controller receives its bonus whenever any player sends an Agent there; revealing a Conflict for a space already controlled permits one troop from supply to the Conflict.

answers.answer: For setup, choose an unused color; place one Rival cube at the bottom of each Influence track and all other cubes in its supply, with no troops in its garrison. Remove the three Arrakeen cards marked 1P, shuffle the remaining House Hagal deck, and place it with its three Agents by the supply; use no Rival Leader or solo difficulty rules. After each First Player Agent turn, Hagal takes an Agent turn if it has an Agent in supply; it does not act after the other human's turn or after a Reveal turn. It has three Agents and never Reveals; its Agents return to supply for the next round. It collects no resources, earns no Conflict rewards, scores no VP, and cannot claim Control. It can hold Faction Alliances.
answers.evidence: Two-player setup and Agent turns specify unused color, Influence cubes, no garrison troops, 1P card removal, three Agents, actions after each First Player Agent turn, no Reveal, and recall. Rival overview says it does not collect resources, earn Conflict rewards or score VP, cannot claim Control, and can take/hold Alliances.

answers.answer: If the indicated space is occupied, keep revealing until an eligible unoccupied space appears. Reshuffle immediately if the deck is empty or a Reshuffle card appears, then continue. Ignore the space's normal costs, requirements, and effects; resolve only the card's icons and instructions. Each troop icon recruits from supply: deploy it on a Combat space, otherwise put it in the garrison. Whenever Hagal sends an Agent to a Combat space, it also deploys up to two garrison troops, even if it recruited none. Harvest Spice follows its card instructions; harvested bonus spice is removed from the space and returned to the bank. For a two-space card, use only the option matching current conditions; if that applicable option is occupied, draw a new card and do not switch to the other option.
answers.evidence: Rival Agent turns: occupied spaces prompt further reveals; reshuffle if deck empty or Reshuffle appears; ignore normal space costs/requirements/effects; troop icons recruit and deploy/garrison by space type; Combat spaces also allow up to two garrison troops; Harvest Spice removes bonus spice; two-space card's occupied matching option means draw a new card, never switch.

answers.answer: At the start of Combat, if Hagal has at least one troop in the Conflict, reveal a Hagal card in turn order; if it is Reshuffle, reshuffle and reveal again. Add its sword icons to its normal 2 strength per deployed troop. Humans then may play Combat Intrigue before Combat resolves. Hagal receives no reward for its rank, but its rank counts when human rewards are assigned. If it wins a Conflict for a space a human controls, remove that Control marker and do not replace it. An ordinary third-place finisher gets nothing; a human tie for second receives the third reward for each tied human.
answers.evidence: Rival Combat: reveal a card if Hagal has a troop, repeat if Reshuffle, add sword icons to 2 strength per troop; humans may then play Combat Intrigue. Hagal gets no rank reward but occupies the rank; ordinary third pays nothing, tie for second gives third reward to each tied human; Hagal winning a controlled space removes the human marker without replacement.
